clue.text: Take some traffic off EEC, upgrading this vessel

indicators.note: Take some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An order to divert part of the traffic away from the European Economic Community while improving some ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of 'traffic' and ends in the first two letters of 'upgrading'; the hyphen of the printed line-break is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup for drinking a hot morning beverage is a small vessel, and 'this' points to the hidden run as the thing being defined.

clue.text: Score's gradually increasing

parts.note: read as a musical marking: the instruction written in a score telling players to get steadily louder

explanation.definitionFit: In music the term marks a passage whose volume builds steadily, so it is literally what a score writes for growing gradually louder.

clue.text: Material, note, used in sack

indicators.note: used in says the note is placed inside the word for sack

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: Cloth, someone remarks, that was used to make a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibre is a material, the threadlike stuff that textiles and cloth are made of.

clue.text: Selfish life is restricted by call-up

indicators.note: restricted by means the word for life plus is is hemmed in by the other piece
in a down clue up means the word for call is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as before a court
go means energy or liveliness, life as in full of life
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-centred existence is cut short by conscription into the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call-up' looks like military conscription, but it splits in two: 'up' reverses the word for call in this down clue, giving ETIC, and 'restricted by' has that hem in the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoistic describes a person putting their own interests first, which is what selfish means.

clue.text: Explorer in 19? Capital!

definitions.meaning: the Genoese navigator who reached the Americas in 1492
the capital city of the state at 19 across, Ohio

explanation.surface: Was the explorer to be found in Ohio? Indeed, and splendid too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of approval, an old-fashioned 'splendid', but it means the capital city of the US state at 19 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The navigator of 1492 is the famous explorer, and the city of the same name is the seat of government of the state Ohio.

clue.text: Author needs publicity put out

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
to oust someone is to put them out

explanation.surface: A writer needs to get some publicity released.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was the French novelist who wrote In Search of Lost Time, so he is an author.

clue.text: American author's royalty

definitions.meaning: Henry ..., the American-born novelist of The Portrait of a Lady
several British kings bore the name, such as the first Stuart king of England

explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was an American novelist, and the name was borne by kings of England and Scotland, so it stands for royalty.

clue.text: Boy of the year?

definitions.meaning: describing a year, as in the calendar of Julius Caesar's reform

explanation.definitionFit: It is a boy's given name, and the calendar year introduced by Julius Caesar is called after him, so it can describe a year.

clue.text: Single-minded work: doctor recorded on no chart

indicators.note: in a down clue recorded on means the doctor is written above the rest

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a doctor
taken as written
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A physician noted on an empty patient chart that his work is narrowly focused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single-minded' usually means determined; here it means a study confined to one subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A monograph is a scholarly treatise on a single subject, so it is a piece of writing with one focus.

clue.text: Author making sound agreement with compatriot

indicators.note: making sound agreement with means the name rhymes with, or is spoken just like, another word

parts.note: a Scot was a fellow countryman of the Edinburgh novelist

explanation.surface: A writer reaches a firm agreement with a fellow countryman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Scott, author of Ivanhoe, was a Scot, so his name is said just like a word for his compatriot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott wrote Waverley and Ivanhoe, so he is a celebrated author.

clue.text: Involve them briefly with cook

parts.note: 'em is the shortened, informal form of them
to broil is to cook under direct heat

explanation.surface: Get them in the kitchen helping with the cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a dispute or difficulty, to involve them.

clue.text: Novel lad — or no?

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Is this book about a boy, or not?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' signals the anagram of LAD OR NO and also names Virginia Woolf's book, whose hero begins as a young man and later becomes a woman: a lad, or not.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's novel follows a young nobleman who centuries later wakes up a woman, so its hero is a lad and then not.

clue.text: Over which Ferdinand and Miranda went to pieces

definitions.text: Over which Ferdinand and Miranda went to pieces

parts.words: Over which Ferdinand and Miranda went to pieces
parts.note: in Shakespeare's The Tempest the two young lovers are discovered playing a board game, moving the carved pieces

explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest the lovers are revealed at a board game with kings and pawns, so they literally went to the pieces of that game.

clue.text: Adding nothing to dimness, instructed thus?

indicators.note: adding means the word for nothing is attached after the word for dimness

parts.note: mist brings dimness or haziness
aught (also ought) is an old word for nothing, nought

explanation.surface: Putting zero onto the gloom, was that how one was taught?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adding nothing' looks like saying it changes nothing; it means tack on AUGHT, an old word for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mistaught is to be taught wrongly, and the question mark hints that a hazy, mist-filled lesson leads there.

clue.text: Craft captained by a Roman nobody

definitions.text: Craft captained by a Roman nobody

parts.words: Craft captained by a Roman nobody
parts.note: Jules Verne's submarine is commanded by Captain Nemo, and nemo is Latin for no one

explanation.definitionFit: In Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea the submarine's master is Captain Nemo, whose name is the Latin word for no man.

clue.text: Runs a vile organization, by no means unique

indicators.note: organization means the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone manages a nasty company that is all too common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' looks like a noun for the vile business; it is the signal to rearrange RUNS A VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something universal is found everywhere, the opposite of one-of-a-kind.

clue.text: Island associated with dancing, largely

parts.note: the Indonesian island is famous above all for its temple dances, performed by dancers in gilded costume

explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' may hint that most of BALL, a dance, is in the answer, but the I is unexplained, so the clue reads as a plain description of the island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island is best known for its traditional temple dance, so it is an island chiefly linked with dancing.

clue.text: Officer in spirit, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken and the answer is what the listener catches

parts.note: in plus spectre, a ghost or spirit

explanation.surface: A police officer is with us in spirit, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in spirit' looks like an idiom for being present in thought; it is IN SPECTRE, a ghost, which said out loud gives the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a rank of police officer above sergeant.

clue.text: Some canvas, say, I spread with salt

indicators.note: spread means the letters are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A bit of sailcloth, let's say, which I lay out with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread with salt' sounds like a kitchen instruction; 'spread' signals rearranging SAY I and SALT, with 'with' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a triangular fore-and-aft sail, and canvas is sailcloth, so it is part of a ship's canvas.

clue.text: Citizen such as Tim, on joining up

definitions.text: Citizen such as Tim, on joining up

parts.words: Citizen such as Tim, on joining up
parts.note: joining Tim and on gives Timon, hero of the Shakespeare play set in the ancient Greek capital

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is a citizen of that Greek city-state, so he is an inhabitant of it.

clue.text: American's greeting bands going around state

indicators.note: going around means the rings enclose the greeting

parts.note: a band or ring is shaped like the letter O, so two of them are OO
hi is an informal hello, especially American

explanation.surface: An American says hello as the musical groups tour the states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' suggests musicians, but these are rings, each an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Pains from needles

definitions.meaning: sharp sudden aches in the side, as after running
the loops of thread made by a sewing or knitting needle

explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sudden side ache, and also the loop of thread a needle makes in sewing.

clue.text: Term for boy or girl

definitions.meaning: the spring term at Oxford and Dublin universities and in the English law courts
a given name used for either sex

explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is the name of the January-to-Easter session at Oxford and in the law courts, and a given name for men and women alike.

clue.text: Conditions in New York and Washington, for example

definitions.meaning: situations or circumstances, as in a state of affairs

definitions.text: New York and Washington, for example
definitions.meaning: two members of the American union

explanation.definitionFit: A state is a condition one is in, and New York and Washington are both members of the American federal union.

clue.text: Shift incomplete test in school subject

indicators.note: incomplete means the word for shift loses its final letter

parts.note: a shift is a loose straight dress or slip, also called a chemise
to try is to test

explanation.surface: Moving an unfinished exam into a different school subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a verb meaning move; it is a dress, CHEMISE, which 'incomplete' cuts to CHEMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry is a science taught as a subject in schools.

clue.text: Seating accommodation in express

definitions.meaning: a long upholstered seat for several people
to put into words, as in ... in polite terms

explanation.definitionFit: A couch is a sofa giving seats, and to couch a thought is to phrase or word it.

clue.text: Provide only half when appropriate

indicators.note: only half means just the second half of the word when is kept

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate, as in due respect

explanation.surface: Supply just half of it at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when appropriate' reads as one phrase meaning at the right time, but it splits: the back half of 'when', then DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue someone with a quality is to endow or furnish them with it.

clue.text: River duck hard to find at first

indicators.note: at first means the word for hard comes before the duck

parts.note: dour means hard, stern or severe
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O

explanation.surface: On this river a duck proves hard to spot at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests a water bird; it is O, a zero score in cricket. The Douro flows through Spain and Portugal to Porto.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douro is a major river of the Iberian peninsula, entering the Atlantic at Porto.

clue.text: Initial advantage for social climber?

definitions.meaning: a start that leaves one up, ahead of the field
a person who has risen above their station and behaves arrogantly

explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in rank who acts above themselves, and split in two it reads as a start that puts one ahead.

clue.text: Disposed to quail, as one always is

indicators.note: disposed means set out or arranged, so the letters are ordered afresh

explanation.surface: Inclined to flinch, as a person always is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed to quail' reads as 'inclined to cower', but 'Disposed' signals rearranging TO QUAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An aliquot part divides a number exactly with no remainder, and the number one does that to every whole number.

clue.text: Christmas decoration altogether pointless at first

indicators.note: pointless at first means a compass point is removed from the front

parts.note: wholly means altogether, completely

explanation.surface: A festive trimming that is entirely without purpose to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' looks like 'futile'; it means lose a compass point, W for west, from the start of WHOLLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprigs of the red-berried evergreen are hung in homes as traditional Christmas greenery.

clue.text: Make no advance with press coverage for brilliant display

indicators.note: coverage means the word for press covers, or surrounds, the other letters

parts.note: to spur is to press or urge on
to advance money is to lend it
O is nought, the figure for none

explanation.surface: Refuse to make a loan, and the newspapers will cover the magnificent show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press coverage' suggests reporting in newspapers, but 'press' means urge on and 'coverage' says it wraps the rest; 'Make' and 'with' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificence or grandeur, the quality of a dazzling show.
